messages:
sophia: local edge dev hit: importing package via pnpm workspace symlink causes module resolution to pick the consumer dist rather than package root. stack points at node_modules/.pnpm/... which is confusing.
sophia: repro: pnpm -w install && pnpm -w build (core) && pnpm --filter app dev:edge
sophia: error: Error: Cannot find module 'core-ui/esm'
ben: This smells like `exports` + symlink behaviour. Some bundlers call fs.realpath and end up resolving into the consumer tree. Check package.json exports and make sure you include explicit import/require targets and package.json export of "./package.json".
raj: Also check TS config: disable declarationMap for packages consumed in-workspace, and ensure sourcemaps include sourcesContent or use sourceRoot so the edge bundler can map back to the package src.
ben: Quick workaround: change app dev import to point at file:../packages/core-ui/dist/esm for local testing. Ugly but avoids symlink resolution.
lina: We've also seen nodeLinker=node-modules remove the issue because it flattens and avoids symlinks, but that's not a universal fix. Document supported node versions too (node 20 enforces exports more strictly).
ci-bot: CI: apps/app-edge failed to start: Cannot find module 'core-ui/esm' (job 256).
sophia: I'll add a short note in the app README with the workaround + open an issue for the edge dev server plugin to prefer package root when resolving workspace symlinks. Will include small repro + CI logs.
raj: For the plugin patch, consider checking isWorkspacePackage(id) and resolving to path.join(repoRoot, pkgDir, 'dist/esm/index.js') when symlinked.
sophia: Thanks, pushing README + issue now.
